lesson.title: Hello, Hola! Meet Sol the Sun Puppet
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Meet Sol, our sunshine puppet! Sol loves to say hello. Wave your hand with Sol — big and bright, like a sunrise!

Sing Sol's hello song with your grown-up:
☀️ ¡Hola, hola, hola! ☀️
Wave your hand and say it too — [[hola]]!
Now Sol has to go. Wave goodbye and say [[adiós]]! Wave big, just like you did for hola.
You said hola to say hello and adiós to say goodbye — just like Sol! Tomorrow, Sol will show you how to say good morning and good night.

objectives: Say hola (hello) and wave in response to a greeting cue
Say adiós (goodbye) and wave when a puppet or person leaves
materialsNeeded: A puppet, stuffed animal, or drawn paper sun to be 'Sol'
A little open space to wave big
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Introduce Sol (any puppet, stuffed toy, or a paper sun you draw together) as today's guide.
2. Make Sol wave and say '¡Hola!' in a cheerful voice; encourage your child to wave back and echo hola.
3. Sing the simple hello song together 2-3 times, waving big each time you say hola.
4. Have Sol 'leave' (hide behind your back or walk away) and say '¡Adiós!' — encourage your child to wave and echo adiós.
5. Repeat the hola/adiós echo 3-4 times with Sol popping in and out until it feels playful and automatic.
6. Close by asking your child: 'What do we say when Sol comes? What do we say when Sol goes?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just hola today and treat adiós as 'the other wave word' without expecting a clean echo yet — one new sound at a time is plenty
Ready for more: have your child make their own puppet wave hola to a family pet, sibling, or stuffed animal to practice with someone new
This is a listening-and-echoing lesson, not a reading lesson — your child never needs to see these words written down to learn them
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a spoken echo activity — success looks like your child waving and attempting hola/adiós out loud, not a written right/wrong answer.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Opens the course's very first ACTFL Interpersonal Communication target (WA-WL-2015.1.1) the way the K-2 band's oral/aural-first design calls for: a sung, physical, echo-based introduction to the two most basic greeting words, with zero reading required.

generationData.instructions: Read each line aloud to your child and do the action together — there's nothing for your child to write today.

rows.problem: Make Sol wave and say '¡Hola!' Have your child wave back and echo hola.
Make Sol hide and say '¡Adiós!' Have your child wave and echo adiós.
Ask your child: 'What do we say when someone arrives?' (hola) 'What do we say when someone leaves?' (adiós)
